practices_evaluation.justification: The test performs multiple distinct 'Act' operations: it calls AvaliaMultMatrizes.multmatrize(...) with a real array and later calls it again with null to assert an exception. This is multiple Arrange-Act-Assert sequences in one method, violating atomicity.
The test uses only local variables and there is an empty @Before scaffold. No shared mutable static/instance state is used within the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The class as a whole does not provide separate test methods for the happy path and the error scenario for the multmatrize operation. Although this method exercises both flows, the practice expects separate dedicated tests (at least two) per method under test.
The test checks a typical DEFAULT_SIZE array and a null case, but it does not exercise boundary values such as zero-length arrays or other edge sizes.
The class defines a helper method createIntArray(int) that reduces duplication and the test follows a clear Arrange-Act-Assert structure.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test contains an explicit for-each loop to check each array element, which increases test complexity and introduces loop logic into the test body. The presence of a loop violates the guideline to avoid loops in unit tests.
The test verifies multiple properties: array length and element values, and also checks behavior for a null input (exception). Assertions go beyond superficial checks.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods in the shown code; tests are active and runnable.
The method Javadoc explicitly references the requirement ID (REQ-MULT-001), providing traceability to requirements.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses a timeout attribute (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which is an explicit performance-related guard; therefore the presence of a timeout counts as an explicit performance-related test indicator.
The method name 'test0' is generic and does not follow descriptive naming conventions despite the presence of a Javadoc comment. Naming should describe the scenario and expected outcome.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method name 'test0' combined with the EvoSuite runner and typical autogenerated naming patterns suggests remnants of code generation; repetitive generic names are a sign of heavy generation.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes Given/When/Then comments and a requirement ID in the Javadoc, indicating deliberate design and prioritization of the scenario.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises public API methods only and does not use reflection or access internal private state; it validates behavior via public calls.
Assertions include descriptive failure messages (assertNotNull and assertEquals with messages) rather than bare true/false checks, and multiple specific assertions are used.
Comments are minimal and describe Given/When/Then; there is no excess commented-out code and the method-level Javadoc documents purpose.
The method contains no use of Random, current time, sleeps, or external dependencies; it is deterministic based on the provided inputs.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only manipulates local arrays and does not create files, modify static state, or persist data; it is side-effect free.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing categorization for test selection.
The method constructs a single object and performs a single assertion; there is one clear Arrange-Act-Assert flow and no extra acts.
The test uses only local variables and does not depend on other tests; there is a @Before scaffold but no shared mutable state in this method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only validates the happy-path constructor behavior and there is no separate test for an exceptional or invalid-construction scenario for this API; the practice expects at least one error-flow test for the functionality under test.

practices_report.description: Each test case must focus on a single requirement or behavior.
Tests should not depend on other tests or execution order.

practices_report.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_report.description: Test cases must check both normal and edge case scenarios.
Tests should validate inputs at minimum, maximum, and just outside boundaries.
Tests should be self-contained and reusable; extract repeated setup.

practices_report.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_report.description: Keep tests small and avoid unnecessary complexity (loops, nested conditionals).
Assertions should be comprehensive and verify relevant properties.
Avoid @Ignore or commented-out tests; keep suite active.
Each test should be linked to a requirement (annotations or Javadoc).

practices_report.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_report.description: Performance/security tests should be explicit and separate when relevant.
Test names should describe the scenario and expected outcome.

practices_report.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation

practices_report.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design

practices_report.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance

Comments should explain 'why' not 'what' and avoid commented-out code.
